design: MemoryPartition is the full ADD v1.3 Part II §2.6 isolation tuple (tenant, organization, domain, sorted compartments, marking, purpose, policy bundle, ontology release, memory scope, scope owner bindings); its digest names every physical partition (content address, lexical table, vector collection). No cross-partition dedupe, index or ANN graph.

RepresentationPointer is a closed record carried both by metadata and by every index entry: memory_version_ref, item_digest, content_digest, representation_kind, representation_version (lexical profile / embedding model pins / content schema), representation_digest (FULL_TEXT: canonical digest of representation_version and the document digest; VECTOR: canonical digest of representation_version, embedding_digest and the binary32 digest of the vector as indexed; STRUCTURED: item digest), partition_digest, marking, policy bundle, scope, deletion_epoch. store_ref is an opaque URN of its digest; backend IDs never cross the ports.

MemoryStoreCoordinator.commit: verifies the AdmittedMemoryVersion and requires the identical record in the admission ledger; validates payload digest, the strict UTF-8 lexical document and the embedding (dimensions, finite, non-zero, digest = item embedding_digest); stages metadata + pointers PENDING; seals content via the ContentCipher port bound to partition/content address, refusing any output that contains the plaintext at any length (bounded reseal) or that opens under a foreign content address; writes each projection and re-reads both its pointer and its indexed body (document / persisted vector) through read_back (never trusts an ACK); then one metadata transaction flips version + pointers to COMMITTED and advances the head pointer only from n-1 to n.

Reads: read_version/read_latest materialise only COMMITTED versions of the caller's authorized partition (absent and foreign versions are the same MEMORY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND), re-verify the stored item and pointers, check every projection is still bound (drift -> REPRESENTATION_NOT_READY) and decrypt + digest-check the content. lexical/vector candidates admit a hit only if its payload is the committed metadata pointer of the same partition and representation version; unbound hits are skipped before occupying a result slot, with a bounded scan that fails closed (UNBOUND_BACKLOG).

reconcile: pending versions older than the grace window are rolled forward if complete (content opens, every projection bound, predecessor committed) or left PENDING and retracted; the following sweeps remove every index entry not equal to a committed or in-flight pointer and every content object not referenced by a committed or in-flight version.

normative_interpretations: Scope owner bindings in the partition are the schema allOf bindings of the item's scope (agent_run_id/task_id, agent_id, team_id, project_id, federation_policy_ref; none for DOMAIN). owner_principal_id is the author and stays in metadata: including it would split TEAM/PROJECT shared memory per author, contrary to scope = visibility (ADD §2.3).
Lexical document = strict UTF-8 payload so the full-text projection is rebuildable from content (change-control §7); non-UTF-8 payloads cannot declare FULL_TEXT.

Canonical embedding digest = SHA-256 over 'ocor-memory-vector:f64be:' + IEEE-754 binary64 big-endian values; OCOR-DEV-0053 must produce embedding_digest with the same function. Embedding generation and model upgrade (parallel representation, rebuild) are OCOR-DEV-0053.
Content-addressed object store realised on PostgreSQL bytea because infra/services.lock.json pins no object-store service; the MemoryContentStore port keeps the backend replaceable.
A changed lexical profile for an already committed version is refused as STAGE_CONFLICT (no in-place representation swap); parallel representation versions are the rebuild path of OCOR-DEV-0053.
Version n becomes visible only after n-1 (head pointer CAS); exact older versions stay readable (history preserved, no in-place update).

Vector body binding precision: Qdrant persists binary32 components, so an exact binary64 digest of the persisted vector cannot equal embedding_digest; the VECTOR representation digest therefore binds embedding_digest (the binary64 embedding, checked exactly by validate_embedding at commit) together with the binary32 digest of the vector, and read-back requires the persisted vector to have exactly that binary32 digest. Embeddings not representable in binary32 (overflow, vanishing) are refused EMBEDDING_INVALID.

Qdrant Cosine collections normalise non-unit vectors on write; the fixture profile is l2-unit, so the persisted vector equals the binary32 embedding (24-vector live check). A non-unit vector under a Cosine collection would be refused PROJECTION_UNVERIFIED (fail-closed), never committed with a different body.

Plaintext-containment check at every length (VF-002): short plaintext can occur by chance inside genuine ciphertext (OpenBao returns base64 text), so up to SEAL_ATTEMPTS=32 fresh seals are tried; a cipher that keeps the plaintext fails closed. The separate foreign-context open makes refusal of pass-through and context-blind ciphers deterministic and independent of length.
raw_output_format: JSONL: una riga per comando/artefatto/osservazione con label, command, exit_code, sha256 dei byte UTF-8 archiviati e output integrale; le credenziali locali generate (valori di .ocor/bootstrap.env) sono sostituite da <redacted:NAME> prima dell'archiviazione e dell'hash, gli originali restano solo fuori da Git; DSN mostrato come <local generated credential>

findings.VF-001: commit read-back compared only the pointer payload; a substituted lexical document or vector under the correct pointer was COMMITTED. Fixed: _projection_bound re-reads the indexed body through the new read_back port method and recomputes the representation digest (FULL_TEXT: document digest; VECTOR: embedding_digest plus binary32 digest of the persisted vector); PostgreSQL read_back returns no body if the tsvector is not to_tsvector(config, document). Applies to commit (PROJECTION_UNVERIFIED), reconcile roll-forward (retracted instead) and read_version (PROJECTION_DRIFT).
findings.VF-002: the plaintext-in-ciphertext refusal applied only from 16 bytes. Fixed: refusal at every length before any put, with a bounded fresh reseal (SEAL_ATTEMPTS=32) so chance occurrences of short plaintext in genuine ciphertext do not refuse honest content, plus a mandatory foreign-context open that must fail (a pass-through or context-blind cipher is refused deterministically).

requirement_results.command: admitted version committed to real PostgreSQL metadata, OpenBao-transit-encrypted content-addressed content, PostgreSQL full-text and Qdrant vector projections; version and pointers COMMITTED in one metadata transaction; every index entry carries the exact closed pointer (item/version, digests, representation version/digest, partition, marking, policy, scope, deletion epoch); receipt links the admission audit; backend IDs never cross the port; durable across fresh adapters

head pointer advances only from n-1 to n (v3 before v2 refused, non-queryable); exact history readable; idempotent and concurrent re-commit converge to one row set; a different representation for a committed version is a stage conflict with zero writes

non-admitted, tampered, digest-mismatched, embedding-missing/unbound/dimension/digest-mismatched and non-rebuildable inputs refused with zero writes on every real backend; refusals carry the admission correlation id

every attribute of the ADD §2.6 isolation tuple changes the partition; separate content addresses, PostgreSQL tables and Qdrant collections per partition; identical text/vectors never cross partitions; out-of-partition reads indistinguishable from absent; ciphertext moved across partitions does not open

Qdrant paused mid-commit: PENDING version with physically present content/lexical entry is not queryable, countable or materialisable; grace window protects in-flight commits; reconcile retracts projections and content, retry commits; crash before the metadata switch rolled forward by reconcile; acknowledged-but-lost and wrong-pointer index writes refused by read-back; repair 1 (VF-001): a substituted lexical document, a substituted vector and a vector one binary32 ulp off, each under the correct pointer, fail PROJECTION_UNVERIFIED before the visibility switch on real PostgreSQL/Qdrant, are not found by either body, are retracted (never rolled forward) by reconcile, and the honest re-commit binds; the binary32 read-back holds for 24 committed l2-unit vectors

forged Qdrant points (fabricated ref, other-partition pointer, marking downgrade, never-staged version) outranking every bound entry and a tampered PostgreSQL lexical row never occupy result slots; reconcile removes exactly them; unbound backlog beyond the scan bound fails closed

swapped ciphertext refused by OpenBao (CONTENT_UNSEALABLE); re-sealed foreign plaintext refused by digest (CONTENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH); metadata rewritten in place detected; committed projection drift blocks materialisation and is not hidden by re-commit; repair 1: document/tsvector/vector body drift after commit blocks materialisation (PROJECTION_DRIFT) and restoring the body restores it (VF-001); a pass-through cipher at 1, 3, 12 and 48 bytes (unit) and at 1, 12 and 35 bytes on real PostgreSQL, and real OpenBao transit used with a fixed context, are refused CONTENT_NOT_ENCRYPTED with no content row (VF-002); chance plaintext inside one seal is resealed, persistent plaintext refused after SEAL_ATTEMPTS; 1, 2, 3 and 12 byte payloads commit encrypted by real OpenBao transit; a payload inside the fixed transit framing ('vault') fails closed (documented limit)

residual_risks: Real PostgreSQL/Qdrant/OpenBao adapters live in the task test module because the backlog allocates only memory/stores.py and the test file, and OCOR_LANGUAGE_POLICY row 8 confines backend clients to adapters/ in src; no production adapter under memory/adapters/ exists yet (no backlog task owns that area).

Policy evaluation, authorized-partition derivation, ranking/score normalization and non-interference beyond partitioning are retrieval (OCOR-DEV-0052); lifecycle-based visibility (revocation/expiry/legal hold) is OCOR-DEV-0055; deletion saga and tombstones OCOR-DEV-0056; embedding lifecycle and rebuild OCOR-DEV-0053; quotas OCOR-DEV-0059.
Committed projection drift is detected and blocks materialisation but is not repaired here; rebuild of projections from metadata/content belongs to OCOR-DEV-0053/0056.

The reconcile grace window protects in-flight commits by staging time; a commit stalled longer than the window can be retracted and must be retried by its caller (fail-closed, never visible while partial).

Payloads that are a substring of the fixed OpenBao transit framing (e.g. 'vault', 'v1', ':') are always found in the ciphertext and are refused CONTENT_NOT_ENCRYPTED (fail-closed availability limit for such 1-9 byte payloads, test_a_payload_inside_the_fixed_cipher_framing_fails_closed); confidentiality is never weakened.
